title: Generate reduced-field FEM curves and WHHM fits
action: Implement the FEM equation for the upper critical field and the WHHM Maki form. Using the representative metallic-glass parameters (λ ≈ 1, Θ_D ≈ 0.017 eV, ε_F ≈ 5 eV), compute the reduced field h for reduced temperature t from 0.1 to 1.0 in steps of 0.05, for each disorder parameter ε_Fτ from {∞ (use 1e6), 2.0, 1.5, 1.3, 1.0}. Perform least‑squares fitting of the FEM data to the WHHM form to obtain best‑fit reduced‑field values. Write all data to the output CSV.
description: CSV containing the raw FEM reduced-field curves and corresponding WHHM best‑fit curves for each disorder parameter, as used in Figure 1 of the original work.
output_schema: Columns: t (float, reduced temperature), epsilonFtau (float, disorder parameter; 1e6 represents ∞), h_FEM (float, FEM reduced field), h_WHHM_fit (float, best‑fit WHHM reduced field). One row per (t, ε_Fτ) combination; all ε_Fτ values are included in the same file.

title: Compute α_H/α_H=0 ratio, T_c suppression, and indistinguishability check
action: From the FEM and WHHM data, compute the ratio α_H/α_H=0 (using the slope near T_c from the WHHM fit and the zero‑field slope from the original FEM). Compute the reduced T_c suppression ΔT_c/T_c0 from the corresponding FEM equation. For each ε_Fτ, compute the maximum absolute relative difference between h_FEM and h_WHHM_fit across the temperature grid. Write the results to the output CSV.
description: CSV containing derived quantities: the ratio of field‑gradient parameters, the T_c suppression, and the maximum curve difference used to verify indistinguishability.
output_schema: Columns: epsilonFtau (float), alpha_H_over_alpha_0 (float), dTc_over_Tc0 (float), max_rel_diff_h_vs_WHHM_fit (float). One row per ε_Fτ value; ε_Fτ=∞ (1e6) produces the Maki limit with α_H/α_0 = 1 and zero suppression.
